title: Sixth, Fifth, Third, Second, First: Neumann Never Gives It Back
title_candidates: Sixth, Fifth, Third, Second, First: Neumann Never Gives It Back
Never Headed: Neumann's Long Climb Ends on the Lisbon Coast
From Two Spoons to the Silverware
The Quiet Coronation of Stuart Neumann
theme: Two untroubled processions at the front — Neumann's first Trophy, Williams's second Jacket, neither man headed after the opening holes — while the four Portuguese courses took the rest of the field apart hole by hole. The story is a man arriving after five TEGs of climbing, told against the wreckage behind him.
tone: house — subverted gravitas: the procession reported with the solemnity of a state occasion, the carnage behind it deadpan and precisely itemised. British English throughout.
opening_hook: Open on Estoril's 8th in R4 — stroke index 1 — where Neumann calmly writes down a quintuple-bogey 9 (b46) that changes precisely nothing, because the Trophy had been settled days earlier; then rewind to explain how a man with two Wooden Spoons and no wins to his name came to be that comfortable.

trophy_storyline.subject: Stuart Neumann's first Trophy: 156 points, led after every round, won by 13
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: Neumann arrived at TEG 16 with no Trophy wins, no Jackets and two prior Wooden Spoons, having finished 6th (TEG 9), 5th (TEG 10), 3rd (TEG 12) and 2nd (TEG 15) — the ladder finally topped out.
trophy_storyline.shape: He opened with 39 at Oitavos Dunes and was five clear by the end of the day; the only company he had at the summit came inside the opening five holes of the tournament, and it was routine. He was the best scorer in the field again at Troia and again at Penha Longa (b43, b28), the lead swelling 5 to 7 to 12, so that Estoril was only ever about the size of it. He closed with 43 points — his best round of the four, and a new personal best of 92 gross at Estoril, 14 better than his last visit — with a quintuple-bogey 9 at the 8th, Estoril's stroke index 1, sitting inside it (b46): a catastrophe of no consequence whatsoever (b01, b08).

jacket_storyline.subject: Gregg Williams's Green Jacket: +66, the best gross round in the field on all four days, won by 16
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: Williams came in as defending Trophy champion with one prior Jacket (TEG 15); he leaves with back-to-back Jackets and, per the beat, the fifth-best Jacket total in TEG history — and still lost the main event by 13.
jacket_storyline.shape: He led the gross from the first evening and posted the best gross round in the field in every one of the four rounds; Jon Baker drew level at Troia in R2 without ever getting past him. Penha Longa in R3 was where it stopped being a competition: Williams birdied the 5th to end a triple-and-double wobble (b25), survived a barren 6th-to-8th (b35), then parred the 11th through the 15th without dropping a shot (b18, b23) for 15 over — eleven better than Mullin — and a four-shot lead became fourteen. At Estoril he signed for 80, a personal best at the course by six, with a quadruple-bogey 8 at the 14th inside it (b03), and took the Jacket by 16 (b02).

spoon_storyline.subject: Alex Baker retains the Wooden Spoon — 127 points, bottom of the race from the first hole, and two all-time course-worsts
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: The reigning Spoon holder makes it back-to-back and three in all, a former Trophy winner who set the worst round ever recorded at Oitavos Dunes and then, three days later, the worst ever recorded at Estoril.
spoon_storyline.shape: He opened with a quintuple-bogey 9 at Oitavos's 1st (b49), added a 9 at the 11th (b47) and bled 11 shots over the closing three holes including a 10 at the 17th (b37): 113 gross, the worst round in twelve prior TEG visits to Oitavos Dunes (cr03), and 10 shots worse than his own last visit there. He was bottom of the Spoon race from R1 and never once climbed out of it, the decisive drop coming at Troia's 13th in R2 amid 13 shots lost from the 13th to the 17th (b33), followed by 12 more across the 11th to 14th at Penha Longa (b19, b26, b44). Estoril's final day supplied a 9 at the 1st (b32), an 8 at the 3rd (b39), 14 shots bled from the 5th to the 10th (b30, b31, b38) and a septuple-bogey 11 at the 12th (b09) for 107 gross — a new Estoril course-worst (cr02), 8 worse than his last visit — and yet the final margin over his brother Jon was only four points (b24).

discovered_storylines.subject: Penha Longa, R3: the field comes apart on the mountain while two men keep their footing
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The third TEG round at the steepest course on the schedule produced the tournament's densest concentration of damage — and it is where both competitions were effectively closed out.
discovered_storylines.shape: Penha Longa had been kind on TEG's last visit: Jon Baker and Mullin both had prior bests of 85 there, and neither got near it. Between the 11th and the 14th the field simply dissolved — Jon Baker took 10 at the par-5 12th, stroke index 17, the second-easiest hole on the course (b34), then 8 at the 13th, 11 shots gone in three holes (b21, b27); Alex Baker took 9 at that same 12th and bled 12 across the 11th to 14th (b44, b19, b26); Mullin found an 8 at the 16th, stroke index 1 (b05), and finished 13 shots worse than his last visit. Williams, meanwhile, parred the 11th through the 15th (b18, b23) and turned a four-shot Jacket lead into fourteen, while Neumann's 39 pushed the Trophy lead out to 12 (b28) — the day the tournament stopped asking questions.

discovered_storylines.subject: David Mullin: 30 points at Penha Longa, then the lowest round Estoril has ever seen
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: A nine-time Jacket winner produced an all-time TEG course record 48 hours after his worst round of the tournament — and it still left him 16 shots adrift in the Jacket.
discovered_storylines.shape: R3 at Penha Longa was a write-off: an 8 at the 16th, the hardest hole on the course (b05), 30 points, 13 shots worse than his previous visit. At Estoril he birdied the 2nd (b22), was still leaking shots through the 4th to 6th until a birdie at the 7th stopped it (b04), then took 9 points from the 11th to 13th (b07) and parred his way home (b14, b10). The card read 80 gross — a new Estoril course record, beating 86 across six prior TEG visits there, and 14 better than his own previous best (cr01) — 45 points and a 15-point swing on R3 (b13); the only qualification being that Williams shot 80 at Estoril the same afternoon, so the new mark was matched on the day it was set, and the Jacket still went elsewhere by 16.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Alex Baker's seven blow-ups are real and are itemised in full inside the Spoon story, but a catalogue frame would make the report about the man who finished last; the week belongs to Neumann's first Trophy after two Spoons — and TEG 15 already ran catalogue.the same season.

why_the_champion_won: Built, not inherited: Neumann was the best scorer in the field in R1, R2 and R3 (39/35/39), beat Williams head-to-head in all four rounds, and closed with 43 at Estoril — even an ordinary round in place of Williams's worst would not have flipped it.
